clue.text: We hear dog with detective, rigorous, in Derbyshire area

indicators.note: we hear says the next word is to be taken by how it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a Peke is a Pekingese, a small breed of dog
DI is a Detective Inspector
rigorous means strict, exacting

explanation.surface: Someone spots a dog out with a no-nonsense detective somewhere in Derbyshire.
explanation.walkthrough: The Peak District is a national park in the English Midlands, largely in Derbyshire.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the upland national park covering much of northern Derbyshire, so it names a region of that county.

clue.text: Expert finally altered travel document condition

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert

indicators.note: finally altered says the last letter of the next word is changed for another

parts.note: a visa is a travel document stamped in a passport

explanation.surface: A specialist has changed someone's travel papers at the last moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally altered' turns the closing A of VISA into O, giving VISO.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipulation attached to an agreement, a clause beginning 'provided that', is a condition.

clue.text: Loving indeed — embracing mother by hill

indicators.note: embracing means holding the following pieces inside, so one word wraps the others

parts.note: ay is an old or dialect yes, an emphatic indeed
ma is a familiar word for mother
a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Truly affectionate: a mother hugging someone beside a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to sexual or romantic love, so it is a synonym of loving.

clue.text: Reads dope about criminal

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone reads up on drugs in connection with a lawbreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the nine letters of READS DOPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckless outlaw, typically a bandit of the American West, is a criminal.

clue.text: Wanders? Not right — remains

indicators.note: Not says the following letter is to be absent from the word before it

parts.note: strays means wanders off

explanation.surface: Is someone roaming? No, they are staying put, rightly.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain somewhere is to continue there without leaving, a synonym of the verb in the clue.

clue.text: Measurement taken in Berkshire town

definitions.meaning: the figure shown on a meter or gauge, a value taken by an instrument
a large town on the Thames in the county of Berkshire, west of London

explanation.surface: A survey is carried out in a southern English town.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure on a dial is a measurement, and the same word names a large Berkshire town on the Thames.

clue.text: Clergyman ignored a comedian film star

indicators.note: ignored says the following letter is passed over and dropped from the word

parts.note: a chaplain is a clergyman attached to a regiment, hospital or college

explanation.surface: A cleric snubbed a funny screen actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Chaplin was the great silent-era comic actor, famous as the Tramp.

clue.text: Reliable sofa, see, has us sorted

indicators.note: sorted means put in a different order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dependable couch, you see, has us settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted' rearranges the twelve letters of SOFA SEE HAS US.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something completely secure and dependable, as solid as bricks and mortar.

clue.text: Those with narrow interest, Noah's Ark possibly, hard going?

indicators.note: possibly means the letters could be arranged another way, so they are rearranged
going means leaving, so the following letter departs from the fodder

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A query whether the Ark was a tough voyage for those fixated on one hobby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going' takes the H out of NOAHS ARK, and 'possibly' rearranges the remaining NOASARK.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang the word is a hooded jacket and, by extension, an obsessive enthusiast of a niche hobby, a nerd.

clue.text: First man from Genesis, worker, unyielding

parts.note: Adam is the first man in the Book of Genesis
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: The Bible's first man and a labourer stand firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who refuses to be persuaded or to change their mind is unyielding, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Bringers of gifts, wines, met here after arrangement

indicators.note: after arrangement means once these letters have been put in a new order

explanation.surface: Present-givers and wines met here once everything was arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after arrangement' rearranges the twelve letters of WINES MET HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi of the Nativity story brought gold, frankincense and myrrh to the infant Jesus.

clue.text: Typical example of English mine, some missing out first

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

indicators.note: missing out first says the opening letter of the next word is dropped

explanation.surface: An English colliery that is a model case, with some people left out early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing out first' drops the S of 'some', leaving OME.
explanation.definitionFit: The perfect embodiment of a type is its quintessence, a typical example of it.

clue.text: Drinker's singular desire to meet monarch

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
will means desire or wish
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A drinker longs only to meet the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drinker's' reads as 'Drinker is': the definition is equated with the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: One who swills is a heavy, greedy drinker, so the word names a drinker.

clue.text: Southern Conservative narrative

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A political tale from a Conservative in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale or account of events is a narrative, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Novel orange car conveying self-importance?

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A flashy new orange car shows off its owner's conceit.
explanation.definitionFit: An exaggerated sense of one's own worth, haughtiness, is self-importance.

clue.text: Place of welcome in racecourse, much-liked

parts.note: Redcar is a seaside town in North Yorkshire with a racecourse
a pet is a favourite, someone much liked

explanation.surface: A warm welcome at a racecourse for a popular figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Redcar is a racecourse on England's north-east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpet unrolled for honoured guests is where a ceremonial welcome takes place.

clue.text: Allow too many in, 500, done with boast at start

indicators.note: at start places the preceding pieces at the front, before the number

parts.note: something done is over, finished
to crow is to boast
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A venue boasts of admitting 500 people, which is too many.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at start' is an indicator on the charade: the number comes last although the clue mentions it first.
explanation.definitionFit: To pack a place with more people than it can hold is to let too many in.

clue.text: A rather special aircraft pioneer

indicators.note: special means made differently, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rather extraordinary figure in early flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Amelia Earhart was the American aviator who first flew solo across the Atlantic as a woman.

clue.text: French symbol in hall I decoded on way up

indicators.note: on way up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A French character is found in a hall where someone cracked a code.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on way up' reads ALLIDEC, found inside 'hall I decoded', from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: The hook under a c in French, as in garçon, is a written mark, a symbol of the language.

clue.text: Reportedly see earliest part of play "Plants"?

indicators.note: reportedly says the next word counts by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: the word see sounds like the letter C
Act I is the opening section of a play

explanation.surface: Apparently someone saw the first act of a play called Plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Desert succulents with spines are plants, and the answer is their plural form.

clue.text: Island men reproduced exactly in California

indicators.note: in places the pieces before it inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers
sic, Latin for thus, marks a quotation copied exactly

explanation.surface: An island's men are copied faithfully in California.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon's birthplace is a large French island in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Fashionable article, European, motor racing feature

parts.note: chic means stylish, fashionable
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A stylish European item turns up on a racing circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight S-shaped bend added to a race track to slow cars is a staple of motor racing circuits.

clue.text: Search net, say — at first dig out material characteristic of feudal system

indicators.note: say signals the words are to be taken as spoken, a sound-alike

parts.note: to surf is to browse the internet

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Browsing online to dig up material about the feudal system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes the opening letters of 'dig out material' to give DOM.
explanation.definitionFit: The condition of peasants bound to a lord's land was a defining feature of feudalism.

clue.text: Lesson has learner becoming good girl

indicators.note: becoming says one letter turns into another inside the word

parts.note: a moral is the lesson of a story
L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A lesson in which a pupil turns into a well-behaved girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish female first name, so in crossword terms simply a girl.

clue.text: Broadcast policy gets company off the ground?

parts.note: to air a show is to broadcast it
a party line is a policy

explanation.surface: Announcing a new policy helps a start-up get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off the ground' looks like a start-up's launch but literally means airborne.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm that carries passengers by plane is a business literally operating above the ground.

clue.text: Office equipment, basic, facing resistance

parts.note: a staple food or item is a basic one
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Basic office kit is being met with resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: A desk device that fastens papers with wire clips is standard office equipment.

clue.text: Uncommunicative soldier

definitions.meaning: the lowest rank in the army

explanation.surface: A tight-lipped serviceman.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved person keeps things to themselves, and the same word is the lowest army rank.

clue.text: Feature of poker player maybe — cards in sequence following another?

parts.note: in poker a straight is a hand of five cards of consecutive rank
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
an ace is another card, continuing the card-playing theme

explanation.surface: A poker player's look, perhaps, and a run of cards topped off by one more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' gives ACE only because the surface is already about cards: another card, an ace. A poker player keeps an unreadable look so as not to give the hand away.
explanation.definitionFit: An expressionless, unrevealing look is the poker face a good card player keeps.
